limitation: 1. Reanalysis rainfall (MERRA-2 PRECTOTCORR, 0.5° × 0.625° grid cell) instead of BMD rain-gauge data
evidence (our numbers): Against independent IMERG: dev LightGBM BSS 0.259 (PRECTOTCORR, 1998+ training) vs 0.158 when trained and scored on IMERG; on the test years the frozen forecasts reach BSS 0.368 vs PRECTOTCORR but -0.003 vs IMERG (ROC-AUC 0.97 vs 0.92); MSESS 0.39-0.42 vs 0.11-0.18. Predictors and target come from the same reanalysis (self-consistency).
effect on conclusions: Headline skill measures the ability to forecast MERRA-2 rainfall; skill against observed rain is much smaller and mostly in discrimination, not calibration. Model rankings are robust; absolute numbers are upper bounds.
future work: Verify against BMD Sylhet station gauges and IMERG-Final; train on observation-based targets or recalibrate on them (Platt/beta calibration, prior shift); report both.

limitation: 2. Single grid cell (24.9157°N, 91.832°E), no spatial or upstream information
evidence (our numbers): All 115 predictors are local surface variables; skill is concentrated in rain memory (≈ 42 % of LightGBM SHAP, 55-70 % of grouped permutation importance); monsoon-month BSS of the learners only 0.09-0.34 and onsets caught 41-59 % at best.
effect on conclusions: Models cannot see approaching systems (Bay of Bengal moisture surges, Meghalaya/Cherrapunji orographic inflow), so they rely on persistence and seasonal state; conclusions do not transfer to other sites without re-testing.
future work: Add neighbouring cells / upstream gradients (moisture flux, 850 hPa winds), ERA5 fields, multi-site or spatio-temporal models (ConvLSTM, GNN).

limitation: 3. Temporal inhomogeneity of PRECTOTCORR (step changes ≈ 2000 and ≈ 2016) and of MERRA-2 humidity
evidence (our numbers): Mean annual PRECTOTCORR 1,925 / 2,970 / 5,377 mm (1981-97 / 1998-2015 / 2016-25) while IMERG is flat (3,680 vs 3,757 mm); Pettitt change points p < 0.001 (Stage 1); test wet-day share 55.7 % vs 49.4 % in development.
effect on conclusions: Part of the 'regime shift' is a product artefact; it inflates BSS vs climatology on test (+0.10 for all models), causes the MAE-type under-forecast bias (-1.8 to -4.5 mm/day) and the under-forecasting in reliability diagrams.
future work: Homogenisation or bias adjustment against gauges/IMERG; train on homogeneous products; report skill vs persistence-type references.

evidence (our numbers): Rain-day share in development: monsoon 96.2 % (0.1 mm) / 88.2 % (1 mm), winter 14.0 % / 7.3 %; test monsoon 95.8 %, winter 7.7 % (1 mm). Only 31 rain-free monsoon days in 2020-2025; 12-16 per 3-year development fold at 0.1 mm.
effect on conclusions: Within-season discrimination is estimated from very few events (monsoon ROC-AUC unstable, up to 0.97 at 0.1 mm); annual scores are dominated by the easy seasonal contrast; occurrence forecasts in the monsoon are nearly constant (P ≈ 0.95-1).
future work: Season-specific evaluation and models, thresholds relative to climatology (e.g. heavy-rain percentiles), more years/sites.

limitation: 5. Under-prediction and one-day lag of heavy and extreme rain
evidence (our numbers): 167 test days ≥ 50 mm (mean 83 mm): forecasts on those days 37 mm (Tweedie), 52 (hurdle), 48 (TiDE), 36 (seasonal+persistence), but 45 / 64 / 62 / 48 mm on the FOLLOWING day; corr(forecast, obs) 0.71 vs 0.87 with the previous day's observation; ≥ 50 mm recall 0.22 (Tweedie) to 0.49 (hurdle); 99.9th-percentile forecasts 50-130 mm vs 190 mm observed.
effect on conclusions: The models are not early-warning tools for flash floods (e.g. the June 2022 and June 2024 Sylhet events); they react after heavy rain.
future work: NWP or upstream inputs, quantile/extreme-value losses, event-based verification (e.g. SEDI), sub-daily data.

limitation: 6. Sample-size ceiling for deep sequence models
evidence (our numbers): 14,214 development days (≈ 39 monsoons) at one site; 115 features (124 days per feature); tuned TFT classifier 412,927 parameters; deep tuning did not transfer from the 2012-14 slice to 2015-19; one TSMixer seed early-stopped at epoch 1 (test MAE 13.2 mm).
effect on conclusions: Deep models are data-limited and seed-sensitive; their failure to beat boosters is a statement about this data regime, not about the architectures in general.
future work: Pool many grid cells/stations, pre-training on large reanalysis archives, stronger regularisation, ensembles.

limitation: 7. No NWP inputs; UTC day; data latency — a diagnostic hindcast, not an operational system
evidence (our numbers): Inputs are day-t reanalysis values only; POWER days are UTC (06:00-06:00 Bangladesh time), not a gauge reporting day (typically 24 h ending in the morning local time); MERRA-2-based POWER data are published with a delay of weeks, so day-t inputs are not available at the end of day t in real time.
effect on conclusions: Skill is that of a perfect-information persistence-plus-state model; operational skill would be lower, and NWP-based forecasts (which see the incoming weather) are the relevant operational benchmark.
future work: Use real-time inputs (GFS/ECMWF analyses, near-real-time IMERG), add NWP day-1 forecasts as predictors, align to the gauge reporting day.

limitation: 8. Non-stationarity and climate / product drift between training and evaluation decades
evidence (our numbers): All test MAEs +1.6 to +2.6 mm and BSS vs climatology +0.09 to +0.12 vs development; ranking stable (Spearman 0.88-0.95); shorter recent-only training windows did not help (win_2010 ΔBSS -0.06); deep tuning on 2012-14 did not transfer to 2015-19.
effect on conclusions: Absolute scores depend on the period; relative conclusions are more robust. A model trained on 1981-2019 is already mis-calibrated for 2020-2025 (under-forecast probabilities and amounts).
future work: Rolling re-training and recalibration, drift monitoring, equal-length era ablations (separating sample size from regime).

limitation: 9. Single test period and selection effects
evidence (our numbers): One 6-year test window (2,192 days, 72 months as bootstrap blocks); tuned CV scores carry fold-selection optimism (seed-0 optimism ≈ 0.003 BSS for boosters); about 84 ablation contrasts without multiplicity correction.
effect on conclusions: Small differences between good models (≤ 0.01 BSS) are not resolvable; only Holm-significant test differences are claimed.
future work: Longer or additional independent test periods, more sites, nested CV.

evidence (our numbers): Strong collinearity (lags, rolling means, humidity variables): single-column permutation importances are unstable while grouped ones are not; PDP and ALE agree in shape but differ in magnitude (e.g. rain_log1p); TFT gate weights rank variables differently from SHAP/permutation (Spearman -0.49 to 0.44).
effect on conclusions: Importances describe the fitted models, not physical causation; only group-level statements that agree across methods are used.
future work: Causal or physically constrained designs, controlled experiments with NWP, conditional importance methods.
